taxonomy.label: Individual or floater
taxonomy.value: Both Individual and Family Floater are supported (depends on Policy Schedule)
taxonomy.quote: The maximum, total and cumulative liability of the Company under any and all such claims during each Policy Year shall be the Sum Insured (Individual or Floater)
taxonomy.plainEnglish: The policy can be issued either as an individual cover or as a family floater, based on the policy schedule.

taxonomy.label: Policy tenure
taxonomy.value: Policy Year defined as 12 months; policy period can be multi-year but exact tenure is per schedule
taxonomy.quote: Policy Year means a period of twelve months beginning from the Commencement Date... If the Policy Period is of two/three years...
taxonomy.reference: Page 10 | Def. 23 Policy Year; Page 14 | Section B-1.8(h)
taxonomy.plainEnglish: A policy year is 12 months. The policy may be bought for 1, 2, or 3 years (exact tenure is in your policy schedule).

taxonomy.label: Renewability terms
taxonomy.value: Renewable except on grounds of established fraud or non-disclosure/misrepresentation (and subject to moratorium/withdrawal conditions)
taxonomy.quote: A health insurance policy shall be renewable except on grounds of established fraud or non -disclosure or misrepresentation by the insured, provided the policy is not withdrawn and also subject to conditions stated under Moratorium clause
taxonomy.plainEnglish: The insurer generally must renew the policy, except in cases like fraud/non-disclosure, and if the product is withdrawn.

taxonomy.label: Grace period
taxonomy.value: 15 days (monthly mode) and 30 days (all other modes); coverage during grace period only if premium is paid in instalments during policy period
taxonomy.quote:
The grace period for payment of the premium for all types of insurance policies shall be: fifteen days where premium payment mode is monthly and thirty days in all other cases.
Provided the insurers shall offer coverage during the grace period, if the premium is paid in instalments during the policy period.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: You get 15 days (monthly) or 30 days (other modes) to pay renewal premium. Coverage during grace period applies when paying in instalments (as stated).

taxonomy.label: Free look period
taxonomy.value: 30 days from date of receipt of policy document (new individual policies only; not on renewals/porting/migration)
taxonomy.quote: The insured person shall be allowed free look period of thirty days from date of receipt of the policy document to review the terms and conditions of the policy, and to return the same if not acceptable.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: You can cancel a new individual policy within 30 days of receiving it (subject to conditions), but not for renewals/porting/migration.

taxonomy.label: Portability
taxonomy.value: Port to other insurers; apply at least 30 days before renewal but not earlier than 60 days; continuity benefits as per IRDAI portability guidelines
taxonomy.quote: The Insured Person will have the option to port the Policy to other insurers... at least 30 days before, but not earlier than 60 days from the policy renewal date as per IRDAI guidelines related to Portability.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: You can transfer (port) this policy to another insurer before renewal and keep waiting-period credits as per IRDAI rules.

taxonomy.label: Adult entry age
taxonomy.quote: Not found
taxonomy.plainEnglish: The excerpt does not specify minimum/maximum adult entry age.

taxonomy.label: Child entry age
taxonomy.value: Dependent children eligible from 90 days to 25 years (if financially independent above 18, ineligible in subsequent renewals)
taxonomy.quote: Dependent Children (i.e. natural or legally adopted) between the Age 90 days to Age 25 years. If the child above 18 years of Age is financially independent, he or she shall be ineligible for coverage under this Policy in the subsequent renewals.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Children can be covered from 90 days to 25 years, but financially independent children above 18 may not be allowed to continue at renewal.

taxonomy.label: Maximum age
taxonomy.quote: Not found
taxonomy.plainEnglish: The excerpt does not state a maximum entry or renewal age for adults.

taxonomy.label: Family definition
taxonomy.value: Legally wedded spouse; parents and parents-in-law; dependent children (90 days to 25 years, subject to dependency rule)
taxonomy.quote:
Family Members means any one or more of the following family members of the Insured Person:
i. Legally wedded spouse.
ii. Parents and parents-in-law.
iii. Dependent Children ... between the Age 90 days to Age 25 years.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Family can include spouse, parents/parents-in-law, and dependent children (with age limits).

taxonomy.label: Allowed relationships
taxonomy.value: Spouse, parents, parents-in-law, dependent children (natural/legally adopted)
taxonomy.quote:
i. Legally wedded spouse.
ii. Parents and parents-in-law.
iii. Dependent Children (i.e. natural or legally adopted)
taxonomy.plainEnglish: These are the relationships that can be included for family coverage.

taxonomy.label: Sum insured options
taxonomy.value: Varies by plan (lakhs): Optima Secure 5/10/15/20/25/50/100/200; Optima Suraksha 5/10/15/20/25/50; Optima Super Secure 10/15/20/25/50/100/200; Optima Secure Global 100/200; Optima Secure Global Plus 25/50/75/100/200; Optima Select 5/7.5/10/15/20/25; Optima Lite 5/7.5
taxonomy.quote:
Base Sum Insured per Insured Person per Policy Year (in Lakh)
Optima Secure: 5/10/15/20/25/50/100/200 Lakhs ... Optima Select: 5/7.5/10/15/20/25 Lakhs Optima Lite: 5/7.5 Lakhs
taxonomy.plainEnglish: You can choose different base sum insured amounts depending on the plan.

taxonomy.label: Initial waiting period
taxonomy.value: 30 days for illness (accidents covered); exception if continuous coverage > 12 months; applies afresh to enhanced SI extent
taxonomy.quote: 30-day waiting period... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident... This exclusion shall not, however, apply if the Insured Person has continuous coverage for more than twelve months.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Illnesses are not covered in the first 30 days (accidents are covered). After you have been continuously covered for more than 12 months, this 30-day exclusion does not apply.

taxonomy.label: Pre-existing disease waiting period
taxonomy.value: 36 months (unless modified in Policy Schedule; optional PED modification can reduce to 24 or 12 months)
taxonomy.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre -existing disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months (Unless specified otherwise in the Policy Schedule) of continuous coverage
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 36 months of continuous coverage, unless your policy schedule provides a shorter waiting period.

taxonomy.label: PED waiting modification option
taxonomy.value: Optional cover can modify PED wait from 36 months to 24 months or 12 months; can be chosen at channel level only at inception and cannot be opted out for lifetime
taxonomy.quote:
2.12 PED waiting period modification... Modification of PED waiting period from 36 months ... to 24 months (2 years)
2. Modification ... to 12 months (1 year)
... allowed to be opted at channel level only and only at the time of policy inception... cannot be opted out in the lifetime of the Policy.
taxonomy.reference: Page 25 | Section B-2.12 PED waiting period modification
taxonomy.plainEnglish: There is a special option to reduce PED waiting to 1 or 2 years, but it’s not something the customer can choose later; it’s only set at issuance through the sales channel and then stays for life.

taxonomy.label: Specified diseases/procedures waiting period
taxonomy.value: 24 months for listed conditions/procedures (not applicable for accident claims); applies afresh to SI enhancement extent
taxonomy.quote: Specified Disease/Procedure waiting period... excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy with us. This exclusion shall not be applicable for claims arising due to an Accident.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Certain listed illnesses/surgeries are covered only after 24 months, unless caused by an accident.

taxonomy.label: Longer of PED vs specific waiting
taxonomy.value: Longer waiting period applies if a listed specific condition is also a PED
taxonomy.quote: If any of the specified disease/procedure falls under the waiting period specified for Pre -Existing diseases, then the longer of the two waiting periods shall apply.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: If a condition is both pre-existing and on the specific-waiting list, the longer waiting period will be used.

taxonomy.label: Maternity waiting period
taxonomy.quote: Not found
taxonomy.plainEnglish: This base policy wording shows maternity as a standard exclusion; any maternity cover waiting period would be in a separate add-on wording (not provided here).

taxonomy.label: Room rent type
taxonomy.value: At Actuals by default unless otherwise specified in Policy Schedule; plan-wise modifications exist (e.g., Single Private Room, % of Base SI/day for Optima Lite)
taxonomy.quote: Room rent limit shall be ‘At Actuals’ unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Room rent is generally paid at actuals, unless your plan/schedule puts a cap (like single private room or a percentage of sum insured per day).

taxonomy.label: Room rent cap
taxonomy.value: Depends on plan and policy schedule (Annexure C indicates: At Actuals for many plans; Optima Select: up to Single Private Room; Optima Lite: up to 1% of base SI/day)
taxonomy.quote: Annexure C... 1.1.a Room Rent At Actuals ... Optima Select Upto Single Private room ... Optima Lite Upto 1% of base sum insured per day
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Your room rent limit depends on the plan you chose. Some plans have no cap; some restrict to single private room; Optima Lite uses a % of base sum insured per day.

taxonomy.label: ICU charging type
taxonomy.value: At Actuals by default unless otherwise specified in Policy Schedule; Optima Lite has 2% of base SI/day as per plan chart
taxonomy.quote: ICU limit (including ICCU) for bed charges shall be ‘At Actuals’ unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: ICU is usually covered at actuals, unless your schedule/plan places a cap.

taxonomy.label: ICU cap
taxonomy.value: Depends on plan and policy schedule (Annexure C indicates Optima Lite: up to 2% of base SI/day; others mostly at actuals)
taxonomy.quote: Annexure C... 1.1.b ICU At Actuals ... Optima Lite Upto 2% of base sum insured per day
taxonomy.plainEnglish: ICU limits depend on the plan. Optima Lite has a % cap; many other plans show ICU at actuals.

taxonomy.label: Proportionate deduction for higher room
taxonomy.value: Yes; proportionate deduction applies on room rent and associated medical expenses if room category exceeds eligibility; special handling for ICU; not applicable where differential billing not followed
taxonomy.quote: Proportionate deduction on Room Rent: In case the Insured Person is admitted in a room that exceeds the category/limit stipulated in the Policy Schedule, the reimbursement/payment of Room Rent charges including all Associated Medical Expenses incurred at Hospital shall be effected in the same proportion... Proportionate deduction shall not be applicable to ‘ICU charges’.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: If you choose a higher room than eligible, the insurer can reduce payment proportionately for room rent and many related hospital charges (unless the hospital doesn’t do differential billing). ICU has separate rules.

taxonomy.label: Default co-pay
taxonomy.value: No default co-payment mentioned; explicitly states no co-pay for Tier 2 treated in Tier 1
taxonomy.quote: No co-payment shall apply if Insured Person from Tier 2 avails a treatment in Tier 1.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: The policy wording does not specify a general co-pay; it also clarifies that there is no co-pay just because someone from a smaller city takes treatment in a metro.

taxonomy.label: Co-pay percentage
taxonomy.quote: Not found
taxonomy.plainEnglish: No co-pay percentage is stated in the provided excerpt (it may be in the policy schedule, if applicable).

taxonomy.label: Co-pay triggers
taxonomy.quote: Not found
taxonomy.plainEnglish: No specific co-pay trigger is stated in the excerpt.

taxonomy.label: Deductible type
taxonomy.value: Optional Aggregate Deductible (once per policy year) for India claims; separate Per Claim Deductible Rs. 10,000 for overseas global cover claims
taxonomy.quote:
Aggregate Deductible refers to a cost-sharing agreement... bear a self -opted amount... once during each Policy Year...
... However, a Per Claim Deductible of Rs. 10,000 will apply separately for each and every claim ... under this cover.
taxonomy.reference: Page 8 | Def. 3 Aggregate Deductible; Page 21 | Section B-2.9(A)(ii)
taxonomy.plainEnglish: You may choose an annual aggregate deductible (you pay that amount first each year). For overseas cover, there is also a Rs. 10,000 per-claim deductible.

taxonomy.label: Deductible amount/options
taxonomy.value: Aggregate Deductible options (plan chart): 10K/25K/50K/1L/2L/3L/5L/10L/20L/25L (varies by plan); overseas global cover per-claim deductible Rs. 10,000
taxonomy.quote:
2.7 Aggregate Deductible# (Optional)
10K/25K/ 50K /1L /2L /3L /5L /10L /20L /25L ...
... Per Claim Deductible of Rs. 10,000 will apply separately for each and every claim ... under this cover.
taxonomy.reference: Page 51 | Annexure C - Plan Chart (Aggregate Deductible); Page 21 | Section B-2.9(A)(ii)
taxonomy.plainEnglish: You can choose from several annual deductible amounts (like 10k, 25k... up to 25L), and overseas claims under global cover have a separate 10k per-claim deductible.

taxonomy.label: Inpatient hospitalization
taxonomy.value: Covered: hospitalization expenses for illness/injury up to sum insured; includes room rent, ICU, doctors, diagnostics, medicines, consumables, implants etc.
taxonomy.quote:
The Company shall indemnify Medical Expenses necessarily incurred by the Insured Person for Hospitalization... up to the Sum Insured specified in the Policy Schedule for:
a. Room Rent...
b. Intensive Care Unit (ICU)...
... f. ... allowable consumables...
g. ... devices ... implanted internally during Surgery.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: In-patient hospital bills are covered for covered illnesses/injuries, up to your available sum insured.

taxonomy.label: Day care treatment
taxonomy.value: Covered (all day care treatments); 24-hour hospitalization requirement not applicable for day care
taxonomy.quote:
iv. All Day Care Treatments.
... the time limit shall not apply in respect of Day Care Treatment.
taxonomy.reference: Page 11-12 | Section B.1.1.1 Other Expenses; Note (i)
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Day care procedures are covered even if they take less than 24 hours.

taxonomy.label: Pre-hospitalization days
taxonomy.value: Up to 60 days (unless otherwise specified in policy schedule; Optima Lite is 30 days as per plan chart)
taxonomy.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 60 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately prior to the date of admission.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: You can claim eligible expenses incurred before hospitalization, usually up to 60 days (some plans may have fewer days).

taxonomy.label: Post-hospitalization days
taxonomy.value: Up to 180 days (unless otherwise specified in policy schedule; Optima Lite is 60 days as per plan chart)
taxonomy.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 180 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately post the date of discharge from the Hospital.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: You can claim eligible expenses incurred after discharge, usually up to 180 days (some plans may have fewer days).

taxonomy.label: Domiciliary hospitalization
taxonomy.value: Covered when patient cannot be removed/admitted or due to non-availability of room in hospital; must be prescribed in writing
taxonomy.quote:
The Company shall indemnify the Medical Expenses incurred during the Policy Year on Domiciliary Hospitalization... provided that:
a. the condition ... could not be removed/admitted to a Hospital.
or,
b. ... taken at Home on account of non -availability of room in a Hospital.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Home-based treatment (domiciliary hospitalization) can be covered in specific situations like inability to shift or no hospital beds.

taxonomy.label: Home healthcare
taxonomy.value: Covered with written prescription and pre-authorization; not available on reimbursement basis
taxonomy.quote:
The Company shall indemnify the Medical Expenses incurred... on availing treatment at Home... provided that:
... The treatment is pre -authorized by the Company...
... This Cover is not available on reimbursement basis.
taxonomy.reference: Page 12 | Section B.1.2 Home Health Care
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Home healthcare is covered only if the insurer pre-authorizes it; you generally can’t claim it later as reimbursement.

taxonomy.label: Road ambulance
taxonomy.value: Covered for emergency transfer to nearest hospital, hospital-to-hospital, or hospital-to-home (within same city), as part of base coverage
taxonomy.quote: Expenses incurred on road Ambulance if the Insured Person is required to be transferred to the nearest Hospital for Emergency Care or from one Hospital to another Hospital or from Hospital to Home (within same city) following Hospitalization.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Road ambulance expenses are covered for emergency/necessary transfers (including hospital to home within the same city after hospitalization).

taxonomy.label: Air ambulance
taxonomy.value: Optional cover: Emergency Air Ambulance up to limit in policy schedule; requires medical practitioner advice; no return transport; does not reduce SI (as per clause)
taxonomy.quote:
2.1. Emergency Air Ambulance... subject to a maximum of Sum Insured as specified in the Policy Schedule against this Cover...
... The amount specified in the Policy schedule against this benefit denotes the Company's maximum liability in respect to the benefit and shall not reduce the Sum Insured of the policy.
taxonomy.reference: Page 15 | Section B.2.1 Emergency Air Ambulance
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Air ambulance can be covered if you have opted it, within the stated limit and conditions (usually only one-way to nearest hospital).

taxonomy.label: Organ donor expenses
taxonomy.value: Covered: donor hospitalization expenses for harvesting organ when insured is recipient, subject to conditions; excludes donor pre/post, transport/preservation, other consequences
taxonomy.quote:
The Company shall indemnify... towards the organ donor’s Hospitalization for harvesting of the donated organ where an Insured Person is the recipient...
Expenses listed below are excluded... The organ donor’s Pre-Hospitalization Expenses and Post-Hospitalization Expenses... organ transportation or preservation...
taxonomy.reference: Page 13 | Section B.1.7 Organ Donor Expenses
taxonomy.plainEnglish: The donor’s hospitalization for harvesting is covered when the insured person receives the organ, but donor’s pre/post and transport/preservation are excluded.

taxonomy.label: AYUSH coverage
taxonomy.value: Covered for inpatient care in AYUSH hospital up to sub-limit in policy schedule
taxonomy.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Medical Expenses incurred by the Insured Person only for Inpatient Care under Ayurveda... during each Policy Year up to the Sub-limit specified against this Cover in the Policy Schedule, in any AYUSH Hospital.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: In-patient AYUSH treatment is covered up to the plan’s sub-limit shown in your schedule.

taxonomy.label: Modern treatments coverage
taxonomy.quote: Not found
taxonomy.plainEnglish: The excerpt does not show the standard 'Modern Treatment Methods and Advancements' section.

taxonomy.label: Mental illness coverage
taxonomy.quote: Not found
taxonomy.plainEnglish: The excerpt does not mention mental illness coverage/exclusion explicitly.

taxonomy.label: Restore present
taxonomy.value: Yes: Automatic Restore Benefit (100% of Base SI); may be once per year or unlimited as per policy schedule; add-on also mentioned: Unlimited Restore
taxonomy.quote:
2.6. Automatic Restore Benefit
The company shall instantly add 100% of the Base Sum Insured under this benefit in the event of an admissible claim
taxonomy.reference: Page 17 | Section B.2.6 Automatic Restore Benefit
taxonomy.plainEnglish: The policy can restore sum insured after a claim, adding back 100% of base sum insured.

taxonomy.label: Restore rules
taxonomy.value: Restores 100% of Base SI when SI is partially/fully exhausted due to an admissible claim; usable for subsequent claims; usable for base coverage and protect benefit only; not carried forward
taxonomy.quote:
The company shall instantly add 100% of the Base Sum Insured... in the event of an admissible claim during the Policy Year due to which Sum Insured was partially or completely exhausted.
... restored ... only be used to pay subsequent claims ...
... only ... Base Coverage (Section B.1.) and Protect Benefit (Section B.2.3) only.
... shall not be carried forward to subsequent Policy Years.
taxonomy.reference: Page 17-18 | Section B.2.6 (main + conditions ii, iii, vii)
taxonomy.plainEnglish: If your sum insured gets used up in a year, the insurer can add back 100% of base sum insured, but it is meant for later claims in the same year and doesn’t carry forward.

taxonomy.label: Restore frequency
taxonomy.value: Once per policy year by default unless policy schedule states 'Unlimited Times'
taxonomy.quote: Automatic Restore Benefit shall be applied only once during the Policy Year unless specified otherwise in the Policy Schedule. In case ‘Unlimited Times’ is specified against this benefit in the Policy Schedule it shall mean that this benefit shall trigger every time an admissible claim is paid during the Policy Year.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Restore typically happens once a year, but some variants can allow unlimited restores if the schedule says so.

taxonomy.label: Restore for same illness
taxonomy.value: Yes, restored SI can be used for same illness as well as any other illness
taxonomy.quote: The restored Sum Insured can be used even for the same illness for which an admissible claim has been paid during the Policy Year and also for any other Illness covered under the Policy.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Restored amount can be used again for the same disease/illness within the same year.

taxonomy.label: No-claim bonus rate
taxonomy.value: Cumulative Bonus: 10% of Base SI (unless otherwise specified) for Optima Suraksha/Optima Lite/Optima Select; Optima Select inbuilt modification 25% up to 100% (plan chart).
taxonomy.quote:
Cumulative Bonus (CB) [Applicable to ‘Optima Suraksha’, ‘Optima Lite’ and ‘Optima Select’ plans]
... a sum equal to 10% (unless otherwise specified in the policy schedule) of the Base Sum Insured ... shall be provided as CB irrespective of any claims
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Some plans give a cumulative bonus increase each year (e.g., 10% per year), even if you make claims, subject to the plan/schedule.

taxonomy.label: No-claim bonus maximum
taxonomy.value: CB maximum accrual limit is as per policy schedule; plan chart shows maximum up to 100% for plans where CB exists
taxonomy.quote:
CB percentage and maximum accrual limit applicable shall be as specified in the Policy Schedule.
...
Optima Lite: "10% of the Base Sum Insured maximum upto 100%"; Optima Select: "25% ... maximum upto 100%"; Optima Suraksha: "10% ... maximum upto 100%"
taxonomy.reference: Page 14 | Section B.1.8(k); Page 51 | Annexure C - Plan Chart (CB row)
taxonomy.plainEnglish: The maximum CB depends on your plan/schedule; the plan chart indicates it can go up to 100% for certain plans.

taxonomy.label: Plus Benefit
taxonomy.value: Available in Optima Secure and some variants: adds 50% of Base SI on renewal, accumulates up to 100% of Base SI; in some plans it's optional; if Plus opted, CB ceases after carrying forward accrued CB
taxonomy.quote:
2.4. Plus Benefit
... a sum equal to 50% of the Base Sum Insured ... will be added ...
... accumulated up to 100% of Base Sum Insured...
... Upon opting for this benefit, any accrued CB amount shall be carried forward to the renewed Policy and thereafter CB benefit shall cease to exist.
taxonomy.reference: Page 16-17 | Section B.2.4 Plus Benefit (and Notes ix)
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Plus Benefit is an annual bonus-like increase (50% per year up to 100%) available on renewal; in some configurations it replaces future cumulative bonus.

taxonomy.label: Secure Benefit
taxonomy.value: Additional SI as per policy schedule; applied once per year; usable after base SI exhausted; not carried forward; available in some plans (e.g., Optima Secure: 100% of base SI; Optima Super Secure: 200% of base SI as per plan chart)
taxonomy.quote:
2.5. Secure Benefit
An additional amount as specified in the Policy Schedule will be available...
... applied only once during each Policy Year and any unutilized amount... will not be carried forward...
... applicable only after exhaustion of Base Sum Insured.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Secure Benefit gives extra sum insured in a year after your base sum insured is used up, but it doesn’t carry over to the next year.

taxonomy.label: 2x cover from day 1 (multiplier)
taxonomy.quote: Not found
taxonomy.plainEnglish: The excerpt does not state an immediate 2X multiplier from day 1; instead it describes Secure Benefit/Restore/Plus structures.

taxonomy.label: Non-medical expenses waiver
taxonomy.value: Available via optional Protect Benefit to cover listed non-medical expenses (Annexure B) for admissible base claims; also states specific exclusion (k) will not apply to this cover
taxonomy.quote:
2.3. Protect Benefit
The Company shall indemnify the Insured Person for the Non -Medical Expenses listed under Annexure B...
Exclusion (k) of Section C.2 – Specific Exclusions shall not apply to this Cover.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: If you opt Protect Benefit (or if it is inbuilt for your plan), the policy can pay for many non-medical hospital items that are otherwise excluded.

taxonomy.label: Consumables cap
taxonomy.value: Consumables are included as 'allowable consumables' in hospitalization; non-medical consumables/items are excluded unless Protect Benefit applies; any specific sub-limit not stated in excerpt
taxonomy.quote:
Intravenous fluids, blood transfusion, surgical appliances, allowable consumables...
...
Non-Medical expenses... Full list of Non -Medical Expenses is attached as ANNEXURE B...
...
Protect Benefit... indemnify... Non -Medical Expenses listed under Annexure B
taxonomy.reference: Page 11 | Section B.1.1(f); Page 32 | Section C.3(k); Page 15-16 | Section B.2.3
taxonomy.plainEnglish: Some consumables are covered as part of hospitalization if allowable; many non-medical items are excluded unless Protect Benefit is active. No separate numeric cap is shown here.

taxonomy.label: Cataract sub-limit
taxonomy.quote: Not found
taxonomy.plainEnglish: No cataract monetary sub-limit is shown in the provided excerpt (cataract appears in the 24-month specified disease list).

taxonomy.label: Knee/Hip replacement sub-limit
taxonomy.quote: Not found
taxonomy.plainEnglish: No knee/hip replacement monetary sub-limit is shown in the excerpt (joint replacement is in the 24-month specified procedure waiting list).

taxonomy.label: Cashless facility
taxonomy.value: Available at network providers with pre-authorization; if denied can take treatment and claim reimbursement
taxonomy.quote:
Treatment may be taken in a Network Provider and is subject to pre authorization by the Company.
...
In case of denial of cashless access, the Insured Person may obtain the treatment... and submit the claim documents... for reimbursement.
taxonomy.reference: Page 41-42 | Section E.1.2 Procedure for Cashless Claims In India
taxonomy.plainEnglish: You can use cashless at network hospitals if the insurer approves it; if cashless is denied, you can claim reimbursement.

taxonomy.label: Reimbursement claims
taxonomy.value: Allowed; timelines: within 30 days of discharge for hospitalization/day care/pre-hosp; within 15 days after completion of post-hosp treatment
taxonomy.quote:
Procedure for Reimbursement Claims...
Reimbursement of Hospitalization, Day Care Treatment or Pre-Hospitalization Expenses Within 30 days of date of discharge from Hospital.
Reimbursement of Post-Hospitalization Expenses Within 15 days from completion of post Hospitalization treatment.
taxonomy.reference: Page 43 | Section E.1.6 Procedure for Reimbursement Claims
taxonomy.plainEnglish: If you pay first, you can submit a reimbursement claim, but you must meet the document submission time limits.

taxonomy.label: Claim intimation timeline
taxonomy.value: Emergency: within 24 hours from emergency hospitalization or before discharge (whichever earlier). Planned: at least 48 hours prior to admission; Home Health Care: at least 48 hours prior to decision to avail
taxonomy.quote:
Notice with full particulars shall be sent... a. Within 24 hours from the date of emergency Hospitalization required or before the Insured Person’s discharge from Hospital, whichever is earlier.
b. At least 48 hours prior to admission in Hospital in case of a planned Hospitalization or decision to avail treatment under Section B-1.2 (Home Health Care).
taxonomy.reference: Page 41 | Section E.1.1 Notification of a Claim
taxonomy.plainEnglish: You should inform the insurer within 24 hours for emergencies and 48 hours in advance for planned admissions/home healthcare.

taxonomy.label: Excluded providers clause
taxonomy.value: Treatment in providers excluded by insurer (published/notified) is not admissible; exception: life-threatening/accident stabilization expenses payable up to stabilization stage only
taxonomy.quote: Excluded Providers: Code – Excl11: Expenses incurred towards treatment in any hospital or by any Medical Practitioner or any other provider specifically excluded by the Insurer and disclosed in its website/notified to the Policyholders are not admissible. However, in case of Life Threatening Situations or following an Accident, expenses up to the stage of stabilization are payable but not the complete claim.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: If a hospital/doctor is on the insurer’s excluded list, claims are not payable—except emergency stabilization in life-threatening/accident situations.

taxonomy.label: Policy territory (India/worldwide)
taxonomy.value: Coverage throughout India; exceptions for certain optional covers like global health cover and overseas travel secure; plan chart shows some plans worldwide including India
taxonomy.quote:
This Policy provides coverage throughout the territory of India, except under Section B -2.8 ... Section B -2.9 ... Section B -2.10 ... B-2.11 ...
...
Annexure C ... ^Geography ... India only ... Worldwide including India
taxonomy.reference: Page 40 | Clause 1.20 Geography; Page 50 | Annexure C - Plan Chart (Geography row)
taxonomy.plainEnglish: The base policy covers India; some plans/optional covers extend coverage outside India (especially Global/Global Plus).

taxonomy.label: Global emergency cover
taxonomy.value: Optional: Global Health Cover (Emergency Treatments Only) for emergency medical expenses outside India; subject to conditions including trip first 45 days rule; per-claim deductible Rs. 10,000; reimbursement normally
taxonomy.quote:
2.9. Global Health Cover (Emergency Treatments Only)
... benefits shall be extended for Emergency Medical Expenses which are diagnosed and incurred outside India...
... We would not be liable to pay any claim wherein the medical treatment taken outside India has not commenced within the first 45 days of a trip.
... a Per Claim Deductible of Rs. 10,000 will apply
taxonomy.plainEnglish: If you opt the emergency global cover, emergencies abroad can be covered (with conditions like the 45-day trip window and a 10k deductible per claim).

taxonomy.label: Global planned treatment cover
taxonomy.value: Optional: Global Health Cover (Emergency & Planned Treatments) for both planned and emergency outside India; per-claim deductible Rs. 10,000; reimbursement normally; India-incurred pre/post for overseas hospitalization not payable
taxonomy.quote:
2.10. Global Health Cover (Emergency & Planned Treatments)
... extended for both planned and Emergency Medical Expenses outside India...
... a Per Claim Deductible of Rs. 10,000 will apply...
... Any Pre -hospitalization Medical Expenses and/or Post -hospitalization Medical Expense emanating from an overseas hospitalization claim but incurred in India shall not be payable under the policy.
taxonomy.plainEnglish: If you opt planned + emergency global cover, planned treatments abroad can be covered, but pre/post costs incurred in India related to that overseas hospitalization are not paid.

great.name: Room rent and ICU at actuals for several plans (no standard cap)
great.quote:
Room rent limit shall be ‘At Actuals’ unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule.
ICU limit (including ICCU) for bed charges shall be ‘At Actuals’ unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule.
great.explanation: Default wording supports 'at actuals' room/ICU (subject to schedule). This is typically consumer-friendly where applicable.

great.name: Automatic Restore: 100% base SI restore; can be used for same illness
great.quote: The restored Sum Insured can be used even for the same illness for which an admissible claim has been paid during the Policy Year
great.explanation: Many restore benefits restrict same illness; this explicitly allows it.

great.name: Post-hospitalization cover up to 180 days (default)
great.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 180 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule
great.explanation: 180 days post-hospitalization is relatively generous (subject to plan/schedule).

great.name: Pre-hospitalization cover up to 60 days (default)
great.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 60 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule
great.explanation: 60 days pre-hospitalization is a solid benefit (subject to plan/schedule).

great.name: Protect Benefit covers non-medical expenses list (waiver of non-medical exclusion)
great.quote:
The Company shall indemnify the Insured Person for the Non -Medical Expenses listed under Annexure B...
Exclusion (k) of Section C.2 – Specific Exclusions shall not apply to this Cover.
great.explanation: Non-medical items are commonly disallowed; this optional cover can reduce out-of-pocket costs.

great.name: Moratorium: after 60 months, claims generally not contestable except fraud (with enhancement rule)
great.quote: After completion of sixty continuous months of coverage... no policy and claim shall be contestable by the insurer on grounds of non -disclosure, misrepresentation, except on grounds of established fraud.
great.explanation: After 5 years continuous coverage, insurer’s ability to contest reduces significantly (except fraud).

good.name: Initial waiting period is 30 days (standard)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: A 30-day initial waiting is common in retail health insurance.

good.name: Day care treatments covered
good.quote:
iv. All Day Care Treatments.
... the time limit shall not apply in respect of Day Care Treatment.
good.explanation: Covers modern short-stay procedures without needing 24-hour hospitalization.

good.name: Cashless available at network hospitals; reimbursement allowed if denied
good.quote:
Treatment may be taken in a Network Provider and is subject to pre authorization...
In case of denial of cashless access... submit the claim documents... for reimbursement.
good.explanation: Gives flexibility if cashless is not approved.

good.name: Optional global cover available (emergency and planned variants)
good.quote: Global Health Cover (Emergency & Planned Treatments)... benefits shall be extended for both planned and Emergency Medical Expenses outside India
good.explanation: International treatment can be covered if the relevant optional cover/plan is chosen.

good.name: Plus Benefit: 50% of Base SI per renewal up to 100%, irrespective of claims
good.quote: a sum equal to 50% of the Base Sum Insured... will be added... irrespective of number of claims... accumulated up to 100% of Base Sum Insured
good.explanation: Provides meaningful increase in available cover over time for eligible plans.

good.name: Preventive health check-up benefit available (inbuilt in most plans; optional in Optima Select)
good.quote: Preventive Health Check-up... [This is an optional cover under Optima Select plan and an inbuilt cover in all other plans]
good.reference: Page 51-52 | Annexure C - Preventive Health Check-up table
good.explanation: Encourages routine screening; limits depend on base sum insured and policy type.

bad.name: PED waiting period is 36 months by default
bad.quote: excluded until the expiry of 36 months (Unless specified otherwise in the Policy Schedule) of continuous coverage
bad.explanation: A 36-month PED wait is longer than some competitors; may increase time to get PED claims paid unless modified.

bad.name: Specified diseases/procedures waiting period is 24 months
bad.quote: excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
bad.explanation: 24 months is a meaningful wait for common conditions (e.g., hernia, cataract, joint replacement) though it is common in many policies.

bad.name: Proportionate deductions apply if higher-than-eligible room chosen (can reduce payouts)
bad.quote: reimbursement/payment of Room Rent charges including all Associated Medical Expenses... shall be effected in the same proportion as the admissible rate per day bears to the actual rate per day
bad.explanation: If you pick a room above eligibility, the claim can be scaled down proportionately, potentially leading to high out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Global emergency cover excludes oncology and some other categories; 45-day trip commencement rule
bad.quote:
We would not be liable to pay any claim wherein the medical treatment taken outside India has not commenced within the first 45 days of a trip.
...
Specific Exclusions... Oncological (Cancer) diseases
bad.explanation: Even if global emergency cover is opted, it has notable restrictions like no cancer coverage and treatment must start within first 45 days of a trip.

unclear.name: Individual vs Floater depends on Policy Schedule (not fixed in wording)
unclear.quote: Sum Insured (Individual or Floater)... specified in the Policy Schedule.
unclear.explanation: The wording supports both, but your exact policy type is determined by your schedule.

unclear.topic: Room rent cap varies by plan
unclear.name: Room rent cap differs across plan variants (At actuals vs single private vs %SI/day)
unclear.quote: Annexure C... Room Rent At Actuals... Optima Select Upto Single Private room... Optima Lite Upto 1% of base sum insured per day
unclear.explanation: Without the specific plan/policy schedule, the applicable room cap cannot be pinned to one rule.

unclear.name: ICU cap differs across plan variants (At actuals vs %SI/day)
unclear.quote: Annexure C... ICU At Actuals... Optima Lite Upto 2% of base sum insured per day
unclear.explanation: ICU limit depends on chosen plan and schedule.

unclear.name: CB applies only to certain plans; other plans use Plus Benefit instead
unclear.quote:
Cumulative Bonus (CB) [Applicable to ‘Optima Suraksha’, ‘Optima Lite’ and ‘Optima Select’ plans]
...
Annexure C... Optima Secure: Cumulative Bonus Not Covered
unclear.reference: Page 13-14 | Section B.1.8; Page 51 | Annexure C - Plan Chart (CB row)
unclear.explanation: Whether you get CB depends on plan variant, not uniform across product.

unclear.name: High aggregate deductible can disable multiple benefits (preventive, secure/bonus/restore etc.)
unclear.quote: Preventive Health Check-up benefit, Secure Benefit, Cumulative Bonus / Plus Benefit, Automatic Restore Benefit, Daily Cash for Shared Room and Unlimited Restore (Add -on) benefits will not be available under the policy if Aggregate Deductible of INR 10 Lakhs or more is in force.
unclear.explanation: If a very high aggregate deductible is chosen, several otherwise-attractive benefits may not apply; this is a trade-off but needs careful attention.

unclear.name: PED waiting period modification is not selectable by policyholder (channel-level only) and cannot be opted out
unclear.quote: This optional cover is allowed to be opted at channel level only and only at the time of policy inception. Policyholders will therefore not be able to opt for the same. This option once selected cannot be opted out in the lifetime of the Policy.
unclear.explanation: It’s unclear in practice how a customer ensures this is applied; it depends on channel setup at issuance.

unclear.name: Adult entry age / max age not present in excerpt
unclear.explanation: You would need the full eligibility section or policy schedule/prospectus to confirm entry age bands.
